name: link
synopsis: int linkat(int olddirfd, const char *oldpath, int newdirfd, const char *newpath, int flags);
description: The link() system call creates a new hard link to an existing file, allowing the new name to be used interchangeably with the original. If the new path already exists, it is not overwritten. The linkat() variant provides additional options for relative paths using directory file descriptors and flags.

parameters.name: oldpath
parameters.description: Path to the existing file to link

parameters.name: olddirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor for oldpath (for linkat)

parameters.name: newdirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor for newpath (for linkat)

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags for linkat behavior, such as AT_EMPTY_PATH or AT_SYMLINK_FOLLOW

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: Write access to the directory containing newpath is denied, or search permission is denied for a directory in the path

oldpath or newpath points outside accessible address space

bugs: On NFS filesystems, the return code may be wrong if the NFS server performs the link creation and dies before confirming; use stat(2) to verify if the link was created.
versions: Linux 2.6.18 and later for linkat(); POSIX.1-2001 with changes in POSIX.1-2008
